summary: Joachim Wach was a religious studies and philosophy scholar who studied at Munich, Berlin, Freiburg, TU Bergakademie Freiberg, Leiden, Leipzig, and Heidelberg. He held posts at Leipzig University, Brown University (1935–1946), and the University of Chicago (1945–1955).

Joan Halifax is a Buddhist and religious studies scholar who studied at Tulane and Union Institute & University under teachers Seungsahn Haengwon and Bernie Glassman. She worked at Columbia, Maryland Psychiatric Research Center, and as a visiting scholar at the Library of Congress.
Joanna Cook is a religious and Buddhist studies scholar who studied under advisor James Laidlaw. She holds a post at Christ's College, University of Cambridge.

Joanna Gottfried Williams (1939–2022) was a history, archaeology, and Indology scholar. She studied at Swarthmore College, Radcliffe College, and Harvard University before serving as a professor at the University of California, Berkeley from circa 1971 to 2003.

Joanna Jurewicz is an Indology, linguistics, and philosophy scholar who studied under Maria Krzysztof Byrski. She holds academic posts as a professor at the University of Warsaw, attested in 2006 and 2026.

Joanna Macy was a religious studies and philosophy scholar who studied at Wellesley College from circa 1946 to 1950 and completed studies at Syracuse University in 1978. She also taught Stephanie Kaza.

Joanne Punzo Waghorne is an Indology and religious studies scholar who studied at the University of Chicago. She held posts at the University of Massachusetts Boston (1975–1983), Bowdoin College (1983–1985), UNC Chapel Hill (1987–2002), and Syracuse University.

Joe Bransford Wilson is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Tibetology who earned his Ph.D. at the University of Virginia in 1984. He held teaching posts at the University of Virginia (1981–1985) and UNC Wilmington (attested 1994–2001).

Joe Cribb is a scholar of history, archaeology, Indology, and Iranian and Central Asian studies who studied at Queen Mary University of London. He was Keeper of Coins and Medals at the British Museum (1970–2010).
Joen Imai is a Buddhist studies scholar who has served as a professor at Shuchiin University, with posts attested in 2010 and 2026.

Joey Hung is a computational and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at the Hong Kong Academy for Performing Arts. He held posts at Dharma Drum Buddhist College and serves as a professor at the Chung-Hwa Institute of Buddhist Studies.
Jogendra Singh is a Buddhist studies and Indology scholar who studied at Nava Nalanda Mahavihara under teacher Uma Shankar Vyas.

Jogindra Nath Samaddar was a history, archaeology, and Indology scholar who studied at Bangabasi College and Presidency College, Kolkata. He held teaching posts at Pramatha Manmatha College, St. Columba's College, Patna College, and Patna University.

Johan Elverskog is a Buddhist, Iranian and Central Asian, and history scholar. He studied at UC Berkeley and Indiana University Bloomington, later holding posts at UC Santa Barbara, Inner Mongolia Academy of Social Sciences, and Southern Methodist University.
Johan Hendrik Kern was a linguistics scholar who held posts at the University of Groningen from 1901 to 1924 and at Leiden University from 1924 to 1933.

Johan Huizinga was a history, archaeology, Indology, and linguistics scholar who studied at the University of Groningen and Leiden University under Hendrik Kern. He held academic posts at Groningen (1905–1915) and Leiden (1914–1942).

Johann Andreas Schmeller was a linguistics scholar who studied at Königliches Erziehungsinstitut für Studierende. He held positions at the Bavarian Cadet Corps (1814–1826), Bavarian State Library (1829), and as a professor at the University of Munich.

Johann Caspar von Orelli was a linguistics scholar who held posts at the Cantonal School of Graubünden (circa 1807–1819), the Carolinum Zürich (circa 1819–1833), and the University of Zurich (circa 1833–1849).

Johann Christoph Adelung was a linguist who studied at Kloster Berge school and Martin Luther University of Halle-Wittenberg. He held posts as a professor at Evangelisches Ratsgymnasium Erfurt (1758) and chief librarian at Dresden's Saxon State Library (1787).

Johann Ernst Wilhelm Osiander was an Indology and linguistics scholar who studied under Rudolf von Roth at the University of Tübingen. He later held posts as a Repetent at Evangelical Seminaries of Maulbronn and Blaubeuren and at Tübinger Stift.
